children.translated_text: A certain [<s>Yakṣa</s>], negligent of his duties due to the weight of separation from his beloved,
his glory eclipsed by a curse from his master, lasting the duration of a year,
made his dwelling among the hermitages of <s>Rāmagiri</s>, where the waters were sanctified by the bathing of <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter (<s>Sītā</s>),
amid trees with cool, dense shade.

children.text: tasminn adrau kati cid abalāviprayuktaḥ sa kāmī
children.translated_text: On that mountain, separated from his young wife, that lover,
having passed some months, his wrists bare from the slipping of golden bracelets,
on the first day of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, saw a cloud embracing the mountain-peak,
resembling in appearance a playful elephant butting against a rampart.

children.text: tasya sthitvā katham api puraḥ ketakādhānahetor
children.translated_text: Standing before it somehow, for the sake of offering [flowers of] <s>ketaka</s>,
the attendant of the King of Kings (<s>Kubera</s>), suppressing tears within, long meditated —
at the sight of a cloud, the mind of even a happy person turns to other [thoughts];
how much more so for one far away from a person dear to the embrace of the neck!
As the rainy season drew near, seeking to sustain the life of his beloved,
resolving to send through the cloud a message of his own well-being,
he, delighted, to that [cloud] for whom he had prepared a welcome-offering of fresh <s>kuṭaja</s> blossoms,
spoke a greeting, its first word being one of affection.
'Where is the cloud — a mere assemblage of smoke, light, water, and wind?
And where are messages, to be conveyed by sentient beings possessed of keen faculties?

children.text: ity autsukyād aparigaṇayan guhyakas taṃ yayāce
children.translated_text: Yet, not considering this in his eagerness, the <s>Guhyaka</s> (<s>Yakṣa</s>) entreated it —
for those afflicted by desire are by nature pitiable [in their failure to distinguish] between the conscious and the unconscious.'
'Born in the world-renowned lineage of the <s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s> clouds,
I know you to be the chief servant of <s>Maghavan</s> (<s>Indra</s>), capable of assuming any form.
Therefore I, become a distant kinsman by the decree of fate, make my entreaty to you —

children.text: yācñā moghā varam adhiguṇe nādhame labdhakāmā
children.translated_text: a request made in vain to a superior is better than one fulfilled by an inferior.'

children.text: saṃtaptānāṃ tvam asi śaraṇaṃ tat payoda priyāyāḥ
children.translated_text: 'You are the refuge of the afflicted; therefore, O rain-cloud, carry my message
to my beloved, from me who is separated by the wrath of the Lord of Wealth (<s>Kubera</s>).

children.text: gantavyā te vasatir alakā nāma yakṣeśvarāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: Your destination is the city named <s>Alakā</s>, abode of the lords of the <s>Yakṣas</s>,
whose palaces are whitened by the moonlight resting on <s>Hara</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) head in the outlying gardens.'
'When you have mounted the path of the wind, the wives of travelers,
their loosened locks held up, will gaze at you, finding reassurance in [your] promise [of rain].

children.text: kaḥ saṃnaddhe virahavidhurāṃ tvayy upekṣeta jāyāṃ
children.translated_text: Who, when you are gathered [for the rains], would neglect a wife distressed by separation?

children.text: na syād anyo 'py aham iva jano yaḥ parādhīnavṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: There is surely no other person like me, whose livelihood depends on another's will.'

children.text: mandaṃ mandaṃ nudati pavanaś cānukūlo yathā tvāṃ
children.translated_text: 'A favorable breeze gently, gently urges you onward,

children.text: vāmaś cāyaṃ nadati madhuraṃ cātakas te sagandhaḥ
children.translated_text: and this <s>cātaka</s> bird on your left sings sweetly, as your companion.
Having formed their rows, familiar with you since the time of your conception,
the <s>balākā</s> cranes will surely attend upon you, beautiful to behold, in the sky.'
'And you will surely see her, a faithful wife, devoted to counting the days,
unharmed — [for] your course is unimpeded — my brother's wife.
For the bond of hope, like a flower, generally sustains
the loving heart of women, which would otherwise instantly fall, in [times of] separation.'

children.text: kartuṃ yac ca prabhavati mahīm ucchilīndhrām avandhyāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Having heard your thunder, delightful to the ears, which has the power

children.text: tac chrutvā te śravaṇasubhagaṃ garjitaṃ mānasotkāḥ
children.translated_text: to make the earth fruitful with mushrooms and fertile,
the royal geese (<s>rājahaṃsas</s>), eager for Lake <s>Mānasa</s>, provisioned with lotus-stalk shoots,
will become your companions in the sky, all the way to <s>Kailāsa</s>.'

children.text: āpṛcchasva priyasakham amuṃ tuṅgam āliṅgya śailaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Take leave of this lofty mountain, your dear friend, embracing it —
marked at its girdle [slopes] with the footprints of <s>Raghupati</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), venerable to men —

children.text: kāle kāle bhavati bhavatā yasya saṃyogam etya
children.translated_text: whose affection, meeting you season after season,
is expressed by shedding hot tears born of long separation.'
'First hear me describe the route, suited to your journey;

children.text: saṃdeśaṃ me tadanu jalada śroṣyasi śrotrapeyam
children.translated_text: then, O cloud, you shall hear my message, a draught for the ears.

children.text: khinnaḥ khinnaḥ śikhariṣu padaṃ nyasya gantāsi yatra
children.translated_text: Where, wearied and wearied, you will rest your step on mountain-peaks,

children.text: kṣīṇaḥ kṣīṇaḥ parilaghu payaḥ srotasāṃ copabhujya
children.translated_text: and, diminished and diminished, replenish yourself by lightly sipping from the streams.'

children.text: adreḥ śṛṅgaṃ harati pavanaḥ kiṃ svid ity unmukhībhir
children.translated_text: 'The wind is carrying off the mountain-peak!' — with such [wonder], by upward-gazing,
wide-eyed, timid, innocent <s>Siddha</s> maidens who have seen your bold [departure] —
rise upward from this place, from the thickets of reeds, facing northward into the sky,
avoiding the insolent thick trunks of the elephants of the quarters on their path.'
'Before you, to be gazed upon like the intermingling of the radiance of gems,
from the top of an anthill arises a fragment of <s>Indra</s>'s bow (the rainbow),

children.text: yena śyāmaṃ vapur atitarāṃ kāntim āpatsyate te
children.translated_text: by which your dark form will acquire extraordinary beauty —
like [that of] <s>Viṣṇu</s> in cowherd's guise, adorned by a peacock feather of flashing splendor.'
'The fruit of agriculture depends on you' — with this [thought], by the eyes of the village wives,
tender with affection, unknowing of brow-frowns, you will be drunk in.
Ascending the <s>Māla</s> highlands, fragrant with fields freshly furrowed,

children.text: kiṃ cit paścād vraja laghugatir bhūya evottareṇa
children.translated_text: proceed a little westward, then again northward, swift of pace.'
'You who have quenched the forest-fires with your rain-showers —
the mountain <s>Āmrakūṭa</s>, with its ridges, will welcome you upon its peak, weary from the road.
Not even a lowly [person], mindful of former kindness, turns away

children.text: prāpte mitre bhavati vimukhaḥ kiṃ punar yas tathoccaiḥ
children.translated_text: when a friend in need has arrived — how much less one so lofty!'
'Its slopes concealed by forest-mangoes gleaming with ripe fruit,
when you, dark as an oiled braid, have mounted its peak —
the mountain will surely assume a form fit to be gazed upon by divine couples:

children.text: madhye śyāmaḥ stana iva bhuvaḥ śeṣavistārapāṇḍuḥ
children.translated_text: dark in the middle like a breast of the earth, pale in the remaining expanse.'
'Having rested a moment on that [mountain], in bowers enjoyed by forest-women,
your pace quickened by the discharge of rain, crossing the path beyond that,
you will see the <s>Revā</s> (Narmadā) scattered upon the uneven rocks at the foot of the <s>Vindhya</s>,

children.text: bhakticchedair iva viracitāṃ bhūtim aṅge gajasya
children.translated_text: as if fashioned in streaks of painted design upon the body of an elephant.'
'From her waters, scented with the pungent ichor of wild elephants, having discharged your rain,
take water whose current is checked by thickets of <s>jambū</s> trees, and proceed.

children.text: antaḥsāraṃ ghana tulayituṃ nānilaḥ śakṣyati tvāṃ
children.translated_text: The wind will not be able to sway you, O cloud, filled within,

children.text: riktaḥ sarvo bhavati hi laghuḥ pūrṇatā gauravāya
children.translated_text: for everyone who is empty becomes light; fullness [brings] weight.'
'Having seen the <s>nīpa</s> trees, greenish-tawny with half-sprouted filaments,
and the <s>kandalī</s> plants with their first buds just appearing, along every shore,
and having smelled the especially fragrant scent of the earth in burnt forests —
the <s>sāraṅga</s> deer will point out your path, O you who release drops of water.'

children.text: utpaśyāmi drutam api sakhe matpriyārthaṃ yiyāsoḥ
children.translated_text: 'I foresee, O friend, even as you hasten for the sake of my beloved,
a delay on every mountain fragrant with <s>kubhaka</s> trees.
Greeted with screams by [peacocks] with white-cornered eyes and tear-filled eyes,

children.text: pratyudyātaḥ katham api bhavān gantum āśu vyavasyet
children.translated_text: however you are welcomed, you should resolve to proceed quickly.'
'Bordered by groves of pale-shadowed <s>ketaka</s> trees with split thorns,
with village shrines busy with the nesting of house-sparrows —
when you draw near, with <s>jambū</s> groves dark with ripe fruit at their edges,
the <s>Daśārṇa</s> lands, where the geese stay but a few days, will be reached.'
'Having gone to their capital, marked as the well-known <s>Vidiśā</s>,

children.text: gatvā sadyaḥ phalam api mahat kāmukatvasya labdhā
children.translated_text: and having obtained at once the great reward of being a lover —
you will drink the water of the <s>Vetravatī</s>, sweet, charming with its thunder along the banks,

children.text: sabhrūbhaṅgaṃ mukham iva payo vetravatyāś calormi
children.translated_text: its waves like a face with a frown.'
'Rest there upon the hill called <s>Nīca</s>, for the sake of repose,
with its <s>kadamba</s> trees in full bloom, as if bristling from your touch —
which displays the unbridled passions of the townsfolk
through [its] stone houses, fragrant with the perfume of courtesans' lovemaking.'
'Having rested, proceed, sprinkling with fresh rain-drops
the jasmine-trellises of the gardens growing on the banks of forest-streams.
[You will become] briefly acquainted through the gift of shade with [women]
whose ear-lotuses are wilted from the effort of wiping cheek-sweat, [and who] turn their faces toward the flowers.'

children.text: vakraḥ panthā yad api bhavataḥ prasthitasyottarāśāṃ
children.translated_text: 'Though your path as you set out northward is circuitous,
do not be averse to the embrace of the laps of the palaces of <s>Ujjayinī</s>.
If you do not delight in the sidelong glances of its city-women,

children.text: lolāpāṅgair yadi na ramase locanair vañcito 'si
children.translated_text: startled by the flash of your lightning-garland, their eyes darting — you are deceived!'
'The <s>Nirvindhyā</s> [river], whose girdle-strings are rows of birds startled by the agitation of waves,
as she glides, charmingly stumbling, revealing the whirlpool as her navel —
enter into the essence of her passion, encountering [her] on the way,

children.text: strīṇām ādyaṃ praṇayavacanaṃ vibhramo hi priyeṣu
children.translated_text: for the first tender word of love from women is [expressed as] a playful refusal to lovers.'
'Past her — the <s>Sindhū</s> river, whose slender waters have become [thin as] a braid,
pale-shadowed with withered leaves falling from the trees on her banks —
revealing her beauty through the state of separation, O handsome one —

children.text: kārśyaṃ yena tyajati vidhinā sa tvayaivopapādyaḥ
children.translated_text: the means by which she may shed her emaciation is to be provided by you alone.'
'Having reached the <s>Avantī</s> country, where the village elders are learned in the story of <s>Udayana</s>,
follow [the path to] the city previously indicated — <s>Viśālā</s>, adorned with <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity), extensive.
When the reward of good deeds of the heaven-dwellers who have gone to earth is diminished,

children.text: śeṣaiḥ puṇyair hṛtam iva divaḥ kāntimat khaṇḍam ekam
children.translated_text: [the city appears] like a single beautiful fragment of heaven brought down by their remaining merit.'
'Prolonging the shrill, sweet calls of <s>sārasa</s> cranes with the intoxication of passion,
astringent with the friendly fragrance of lotuses blooming at dawn —
there the breeze of the <s>Siprā</s> river, agreeable to the limbs, removes the languor of love-making,
like a dearest lover, coaxing with entreaties.'
'Your body nourished by the incense-smoke of hair-dressing wafting through latticed windows,
offered the tribute of dance by the household peacocks, out of kinship's affection —
in the flower-fragrant palaces of that [city], weary within from the journey,'
having spent the night on the palace balconies marked with the lac-dye from the feet of graceful women,

children.text: bhartuḥ kaṇṭhacchavir iti gaṇaiḥ sādaraṃ vīkṣyamāṇaḥ
children.translated_text: being gazed upon with reverence by the <s>Gaṇas</s> (attendants) who think, "This is the luster of our Lord's throat,"
you should proceed to the sacred abode of <s>Caṇḍeśvara</s>, the guru of the three worlds,
whose gardens are shaken by the breezes of the <s>Gandhavatī</s> river, fragrant with the pollen of blue lotuses,
and by winds made cool from the bathing of young women absorbed in water-play.

children.text: apy anyasmiñ jaladhara mahākālam āsādya kāle
children.translated_text: Moreover, O cloud, having reached <s>Mahākāla</s> at the time of another occasion,

children.text: sthātavyaṃ te nayanaviṣayaṃ yāvad atyeti bhānuḥ
children.translated_text: you must linger there until the sun passes beyond the range of sight,
performing the praiseworthy evening offering of drum-beats for the Trident-bearer —
you will obtain the full reward of your deep rumblings.
There, the courtesans, with anklets jingling at each step, their hands weary
from playfully waving <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks) whose folds gleam with the luster of jewels,
having received from you the first raindrops of the monsoon, delightful as the touch of fingernails,
will cast upon you sidelong glances as long as a line of bees.
Afterward, having settled in a circle upon the lofty grove of trees that spread like arms,
bearing the twilight radiance, red as a fresh <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) blossom,
at the commencement of the dance, fulfill <s>Paśupati's</s> (Śiva's) desire for a fresh elephant-skin —
watched by <s>Bhavānī</s> whose eyes are still with calmed agitation, gazing with devotion.
There at night, as women go to the dwellings of their lovers,
when the royal highway is blocked with darkness so thick it could be pierced by a needle,
illuminate the earth with your lightning, smooth as a streak on a golden touchstone —

children.text: toyotsargastanitamukharo mā sma bhūr viklavās tāḥ
children.translated_text: but do not, O thunder-voiced one releasing rain, frighten those women.
Having spent the night on some rooftop where pigeons are asleep,
your lightning-wife wearied from prolonged love-play,

children.text: dṛṣṭe sūrye punar api bhavān vāhayed adhvaśeṣaṃ
children.translated_text: when the sun appears, you should again carry on with the remainder of your journey —
for those who have undertaken the tasks of friends never falter.
At that hour, when the tears in the eyes of women betrayed by their lovers

children.text: śāntiṃ neyaṃ praṇayibhir ato vartma bhānos tyajāśu
children.translated_text: must be stilled by their suitors — therefore quickly leave the path of the sun,
for even he, returning to wipe the dew-tears from the lotus-face of the water-lily pond,
would be greatly jealous if you obstructed his rays.
Into the clear waters of that deep river, serene as a tranquil mind,
even your shadow-form, naturally charming, will gain entry;

children.text: tasmād asyāḥ kumudaviśadāny arhasi tvaṃ na dhairyān
children.translated_text: therefore you should not, out of indifference, render fruitless
her glances, white as <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotuses), made playful by the darting of fish.

children.text: tasyāḥ kiṃ cit karadhṛtam iva prāptavānīraśākhaṃ
children.translated_text: Having stolen her blue water-garment, clinging somewhat to the <s>vīra</s>-tree branches on the bank as if held by a hand,
leaving her hips and slopes exposed,

children.text: prasthānaṃ te katham api sakhe lambamānasya bhāvi
children.translated_text: your departure from her, O friend, though lingering, will somehow come about —
for who, having known her pleasures, is able to abandon one whose thighs are laid bare?
The cool wind, made delightful by contact with the fragrance of earth moistened by your showers,
sweet-sounding through the openings of streams, drunk in by elephants,

children.text: nīcair vāsyaty upajigamiṣor devapūrvaṃ giriṃ te
children.translated_text: will blow gently, ripening the wild figs of the forest,
as you desire to ascend the mountain sacred to the gods.
There, having made yourself a cloud of flowers for <s>Skanda</s>, whose fixed abode is there,
bathe him with showers of blossoms, O you who are like the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s> flowing from the mountain —
for the protection of <s>Vāsava's</s> (Indra's) armies, borne by the crescent-moon-bearer,

children.text: atyādityaṃ hutavahamukhe saṃbhṛtaṃ tadd hi tejaḥ
children.translated_text: that radiance was gathered in the mouth of <s>Hutavaha</s> (the fire-god), surpassing the sun itself.
His peacock's tail-feather, encircled by rings of light, which has fallen —
<s>Bhavānī</s> in her motherly love places it at her ear, like a blue-lotus petal;
that peacock, its eyes washed bright by the luster of <s>Hara's</s> (Śiva's) moon,
you should make dance with your thunder, deep as a mountain's embrace.
Having worshipped <s>Śaravaṇabhava</s> (Skanda, born in the reed-grove), that god, and having crossed beyond the path,
with the way cleared by <s>Siddha</s> couples playing <s>vīṇās</s>, fearful of water-drops,
you should descend, honoring the fame of <s>Rantideva</s>,
which has taken the form of a river-current on earth, born from the offering of <s>Surabhī's</s> calf.

children.text: tvayy ādātuṃ jalam avanate śārṅgiṇo varṇacaure
children.translated_text: When you, the stealer of colors, bend down to take water from that river of <s>Śārṅgin</s> (Viṣṇu),

children.text: tasyāḥ sindhoḥ pṛthum api tanuṃ dūrabhāvāt pravāham
children.translated_text: those traveling through the sky, bending their gaze from afar, will see
even her broad and slender flow, made distant by your presence,
as a single strand of pearls upon the earth, with a great sapphire at its center.
Having crossed her, proceed onward, making yourself a mirror
for the curiosity of the women of <s>Daśapura</s>, whose familiar brow-creeper movements,
whose eyes flash with dark-gazelle brilliance above their lashes,
and whose beauty rivals the bees that follow thrown <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) blossoms.
Passing over the province of <s>Brahmāvarta</s> with your shadow below,
you should visit that <s>Kaurava</s> field, stained by the slaughter of warriors —
where <s>Gāṇḍīvadhanvā</s> (Arjuna, wielder of the Gāṇḍīva bow), with hundreds of sharp arrows,

children.text: dhārāpātais tvam iva kamalāny abhyavarṣan mukhāni
children.translated_text: rained upon the faces of kings like you rain upon lotuses with your torrents.
Abandoning the beloved liquor marked by the glances of <s>Revatī's</s> eyes,
<s>Lāṅgalī</s> (Balarāma), turning away from battle out of affection for kinsmen, resorted to those rivers;

children.text: kṛtvā tāsām abhigamam apāṃ saumya sārasvatīnām
children.translated_text: having bathed in those <s>Sārasvatī</s> waters, O gentle one,

children.text: antaḥśuddhas tvam asi bhavitā varṇamātreṇa kṛṣṇaḥ
children.translated_text: you will become pure within, though dark in color alone — like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
From there, go to the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s>, descended from the king of mountains,
with flowing water beside the bank — the stairway to heaven of <s>Sagara's</s> sons,
she who, as if laughing with foam at the furrowed brow of <s>Gaurī's</s> face,
seized the hair of <s>Śambhu</s> with her wave-hands clinging to the moon.

children.text: tasyāḥ pātuṃ suragaja iva vyomni paścārdhalambī
children.translated_text: If you, hanging over the sky from behind like <s>Airāvata</s> (Indra's elephant) drinking,

children.text: tvaṃ ced acchasphaṭikaviśadaṃ tarkayes tiryag ambhaḥ
children.translated_text: were to draw her water sideways, clear as transparent crystal,

children.text: saṃsarpantyā sapadi bhavataḥ srotasi cchāyayā sā
children.translated_text: then your shadow gliding swiftly along her current
would create a lovely semblance of a confluence with the <s>Yamunā</s> in an unexpected place.
Having reached that mountain, white with snow, the source of that very river,

children.text: tasyā eva prabhavam acalaṃ prāpya gauraṃ tuṣāraiḥ
children.translated_text: its rocks made fragrant by the musk-scent of deer resting upon them,
seated upon its peak, you will proclaim — as a remedy for the weariness of your journey —
a splendor comparable to the mud churned up by the bright bull of the three-eyed god.
If upon that mountain a forest fire, born from the friction of straight <s>śāla</s>-tree trunks,
its burden of <s>cāmarī</s> (yak) tail-hair singed by flying sparks, should harass it in the wind,
you ought to quench it fully with a thousand streams of water —
for the wealth of the noble bears fruit in relieving the distress of the afflicted.

children.text: ye tvāṃ muktadhvanim asahanāḥ svāṅgabhaṅgāya tasmin
children.translated_text: Those <s>śarabhas</s> (eight-legged beasts) who, unable to bear your thunderous sound, will in their arrogant frenzy
attempt to leap upon you — the unreachable — to break their own limbs upon that mountain,
you should scatter them with your roaring laughter of tumultuous hailstorms —

children.text: ke vā na syuḥ paribhavapadaṃ niṣphalārambhayatnāḥ
children.translated_text: for who would not become an object of contempt when their efforts are fruitless?
There, upon the rock bearing the clearly visible footprint of the crescent-crowned one,
to which the <s>Siddhas</s> perpetually bring offerings, you should reverently circumambulate;
for those who, upon seeing it, are freed from sin through the cessation of the senses,
become capable, with firm faith, of attaining the rank of his eternal attendants.
The <s>kīcaka</s> (bamboo) stalks sound sweetly as they are filled by the winds,
the victory over the three cities is sung by passionate <s>Kinnarī</s> women —

children.text: nirhrādī te muraja iva cet kandareṣu dhvaniḥ syāt
children.translated_text: if your rumbling in the caves were like a <s>muraja</s> (drum),

children.text: saṃgītārtho nanu paśupates tatra bhāvī samastaḥ
children.translated_text: then the entire musical ensemble for <s>Paśupati</s> (Śiva) would be complete there.

children.text: prāleyādrer upataṭam atikramya tāṃs tān viśeṣān
children.translated_text: Crossing the slopes of the snow-mountain with their various wonders,
through <s>Krauñcarandhra</s> (the Krauñca pass), the gateway of the swans, the path of <s>Bhṛgupati's</s> (Paraśurāma's) glory,
you should follow the northern direction, splendid in your lateral expanse,
dark like the upraised foot of <s>Viṣṇu</s> striving to subdue <s>Bali</s>.
Having traveled upward beyond the mountain-passes, whose plateaus were heaved by the arms of the ten-headed one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>),
you shall be a guest of <s>Kailāsa</s>, the mirror of the celestial women —

children.text: śṛṅgocchrāyaiḥ kumudaviśadair yo vitatya sthitaḥ khaṃ
children.translated_text: which, stretching across the sky with its white peaks, like <s>kumuda</s> (white lotuses),
stands like the laughter of <s>Tryambaka</s> (the three-eyed Śiva) heaped in every direction.
I foresee, when you rest upon its slopes, dark as glossy collyrium,
the charming spectacle that will arise with that mountain,
white as the freshly cut tusk of an elephant —
as if a dark garment were draped upon the shoulder of <s>Halabhṛt</s> (Balarāma, the plough-bearer).
If <s>Gaurī</s>, having set aside the serpent-bracelet there, her hand taken by <s>Śambhu</s>,

children.text: krīḍāśaile yadi ca viharet pādacāreṇa gaurī
children.translated_text: should stroll on foot upon that pleasure-mountain,
fashion yourself into steps with graceful curves, your inner waters held still,
providing the comfort of a gentle touch to her feet as she ascends.
There the celestial maidens will surely lead you,
spouting water struck from their bracelets and thunderbolts, into serving as their fountain-house;

children.text: tābhyo mokṣas tava yadi sakhe gharmalabdhasya na syāt
children.translated_text: if, O friend, there be no release for you, scorched by summer's heat,
then frighten those playful ones with your thunder, harsh to the ear.
Drawing the water of <s>Mānasa</s> lake, where golden lotuses bloom,
gratifying for a moment <s>Airāvaṇa</s> (Indra's elephant) with the pleasure of your veil across his face,
shaking the garments draped on the <s>Kalpavṛkṣas</s> (wish-fulfilling trees) with your moist, spray-laden winds,
you should enter that lord of mountains, merging with its shadows, crystal-clear.
Upon its lap, you will see <s>Alakā</s>, her garment of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> loosely draped, as if upon a lover —

children.text: na tvaṃ dṛṣṭvā na punar alakāṃ jñāsyase kāmacārin
children.translated_text: having seen her, O you who roam at will, you shall not fail to recognize her,

children.text: yā vaḥ kāle vahati salilodgāram uccairvimānā
children.translated_text: she who at your season lifts up showers of water from her lofty palaces,
like a beautiful woman wearing a hair-ornament of cloud-clusters strung with pearls.
Her graceful women, lightning-attended, bearing the rainbow, adorned with pictures,
beating <s>murajas</s> (drums) for song, rich and deep in sound,
With waters within, with floors made of gems, towering with peaks that kiss the clouds,

children.text: prāsādās tvāṃ tulayitum alaṃ yatra tais tair viśeṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: the mansions there are well able to rival you, O cloud, with their various splendors.
A playful lotus in hand, hair entwined with young <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) blossoms,
the beauty of their faces made pale by the pollen of <s>lodhra</s> flowers,
fresh <s>kuravaka</s> blooms in the coils of their hair, lovely <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers at their ears,

children.text: sīmante ca tvadupagamajaṃ yatra nīpaṃ vadhūnām
children.translated_text: and in the parting of their hair, <s>nīpa</s> (kadamba) flowers born of your arrival — such are the women there.
Where the <s>Yakṣas</s>, having ascended terrace-halls of white gems,
adorned with patterns of light-shadows and flowers, accompanied by the finest women,
savor the wine that is the fruit of love, produced by the <s>Kalpavṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling trees),
while you gently sound upon their lotus-drums with your deep rumbling.
Where, for the women embraced by the sighing arms of their beloveds,
the bodily languor born of lovemaking, as they recline upon nets of threads —
is dispelled by moonbeams made bright by the passing of your obstruction,
and by the <s>candrakānta</s> (moonstones) dripping with bursting drops of water.
Where, carried by their constant motion to the upper terraces of aerial palaces,
instantly producing the defect of water-drops upon the paintings,

children.text: śaṅkāspṛṣṭā iva jalamucas tvādṛśā yatra jālair
children.translated_text: clouds resembling you, O cloud, as if touched by suspicion, emerge through latticed windows,
tattered and skilled in imitating the belching of smoke.
Where, when their eager-handed lovers tug at the garments
of <s>Yakṣa</s> women, loosened by the untying of the girdle-knot,
even though the gem-lamps with towering flames stand right before them,
the fistful of powder flung by the bashful women fails in its purpose.
Where, by <s>mandāra</s> flowers fallen from the swaying of their gait,
by petal-fragments of golden lotuses slipped from their ears,
by nets of pearls and necklaces whose strings broke from the pressure of their breasts,

children.text: naiśo mārgaḥ savitur udaye sūcyate kāminīnām
children.translated_text: the nighttime path of amorous women is revealed at sunrise.

children.text: matvā devaṃ dhanapatisakhaṃ yatra sākṣād vasantaṃ
children.translated_text: Where, regarding the god <s>Kubera's</s> friend as <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring) himself in person,

children.text: prāyaś cāpaṃ na vahati bhayān manmathaḥ ṣaṭpadajyam
children.translated_text: <s>Manmatha</s> (the Love-god) mostly does not carry his bow strung with bees out of fear;
his enterprise is accomplished entirely by the coquetries of clever women,
whose glances, dispatched with furrowed brows, never miss their amorous targets.
There, to the north of <s>Kubera's</s> palace, stands my dwelling,

children.text: dūrāl lakṣyaṃ tad amaradhanuś cāruṇā toraṇena
children.translated_text: recognizable from afar by its lovely gateway, bright as a rainbow.
In its garden, planted by my own hand and nurtured by my beloved,
stands a young <s>mandāra</s> tree, bowing with clusters within arm's reach.
And in it there is a pool with steps fashioned of emerald slabs,
studded with golden lotus buds on smooth stalks of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli);
in whose waters the <s>haṃsas</s> (royal swans), having made their abode, with <s>Mānasa</s> lake so near,

children.text: nādhyāsyanti vyapagataśucas tvām api prekṣya haṃsāḥ
children.translated_text: will not resort to it, their grief dispelled, even upon seeing you.
On its bank, a pleasure-hill built with peaks of fine <s>indranīla</s> (sapphires),
beautiful to behold with its covering of golden plantain trees —

children.text: madgehinyāḥ priya iti sakhe cetasā kātareṇa
children.translated_text: that very hill I remember with an anxious heart, O friend,
seeing you with lightning flickering at your side, like my beloved.
And here stands a red <s>aśoka</s> with trembling young shoots, and a lovely <s>kesara</s> tree,
both near the <s>kuravaka</s> hedge and the <s>mādhavī</s> bower;

children.text: ekaḥ sakhyās tava saha mayā vāmapādābhilāṣī
children.translated_text: the one craves the touch of her left foot, as my companion,
the other desires the wine of her mouth, under the pretext of a pregnancy-craving.
And between them, a golden perch with a crystal slab,
set at its base with gems of the soft lustre of young bamboo;
upon which my beloved used to dance, beautiful with the tinkling of her bracelets keeping time —

children.text: yām adhyāste divasavigame nīlakaṇṭhaḥ suhṛd vaḥ
children.translated_text: that perch a peacock, your friend, mounts at the close of day.
By these signs stored in your heart, O noble one, you shall recognize my house,
and seeing the figures of a conch and lotus painted beside the door.
Its splendor is now surely diminished by my absence —

children.text: sūryāpāye na khalu kamalaṃ puṣyati svām abhikhyām
children.translated_text: indeed, the lotus does not maintain its glory when the sun departs.
Having quickly assumed the slenderness of a young elephant for swift descent,
and alighting on the lovely ridge of the pleasure-hill described first,
you should cast into the inner chamber a faint, intermittent light,
a flash of lightning resembling the glimmering of a swarm of fireflies.
Slender, dark-complexioned, with teeth like pointed buds, her lower lip like a ripe <s>bimba</s> fruit,
narrow at the waist, with the glance of a startled doe, deep-naveled,
slow in her gait from the weight of her hips, slightly bent forward by her breasts —

children.text: yā tatra syād yuvativiṣaye sṛṣṭir ādyeva dhātuḥ
children.translated_text: she who is there is, as it were, the Creator's first invention among womankind.

children.text: tāṃ jānīyāḥ parimitakathāṃ jīvitaṃ me dvitīyaṃ
children.translated_text: Know her — she of measured words — as my second life,
alone, like a <s>cakravākī</s> (ruddy goose) when I, her companion, am far away.

children.text: gāḍhotkaṇṭhāṃ guruṣu divaseṣv eṣu gacchatsu bālāṃ
children.translated_text: Deeply longing as these heavy days pass by, that young woman —
I imagine her to be like a lotus pond crushed by winter, or perhaps in some other guise.
Surely her face, its eyes swollen from intense weeping, many
sighs having chapped and discolored her lower lip,
resting on her hand, its beauty only half-revealed through hanging locks of hair,
bears the wan look of the moon when its radiance is dimmed by your approach.

children.text: āloke te nipatati purā sā balivyākulā vā
children.translated_text: At the sight of you she may be busy with an offering of flowers,
or drawing a likeness of me, the meaning conveyed through the emaciated form of separation,
or asking the caged <s>sārikā</s> (mynah bird), sweet of voice:

children.text: kac cid bhartuḥ smarasi rasike tvaṃ hi tasya priyeti
children.translated_text: 'Do you remember your master, O passionate one? For you were dear to him.'

children.text: utsaṅge vā malinavasane saumya nikṣipya vīṇāṃ
children.translated_text: Or, O gentle one, having placed the <s>vīṇā</s> on her lap covered in soiled garments,
wishing to sing a song composed with words bearing my name,

children.text: tantrīr ārdrā nayanasalilaiḥ sārayitvā kathaṃ cid
children.translated_text: having somehow drawn sound from the strings, moistened by her tears,

children.text: bhūyo bhūyaḥ svayam api kṛtāṃ mūrcchanāṃ vismarantī
children.translated_text: she forgets again and again the melody she herself composed.
Or perhaps she is counting the remaining months of separation's appointed term,
laying upon the ground, one by one, flowers dropped from the threshold,
or savoring in her heart a remembered beginning of our union —
for these are mostly the diversions of women in the absence of their lovers.

children.text: savyāpārām ahani na tathā pīḍayed viprayogaḥ
children.translated_text: The pain of separation does not torment her so much during the day, when she is occupied;

children.text: śaṅke rātrau gurutaraśucaṃ nirvinodāṃ sakhīṃ te
children.translated_text: I fear your friend at night bears heavier grief, bereft of diversion.

children.text: matsaṃdeśaiḥ sukhayitum ataḥ paśya sādhvīṃ niśīthe
children.translated_text: Therefore, seek to comfort that faithful woman at midnight with my message;
approach her, sleepless, standing near the window on her ground-level bed.
Grown yet thinner from separation, lying on one side upon the bed of longing,
like the sliver of the moon at the eastern horizon, reduced to a mere digit —

children.text: nītā rātriḥ kṣaṇa iva mayā sārdham icchāratair yā
children.translated_text: the night that was spent like an instant with me in the pleasures of desire,
that same night, now vast with separation, she passes with hot tears.
Tossing aside with her sighs her tangled hair, which surely hangs down to her cheeks,
rough and unwashed since her last pure bath,
'How shall union with my beloved come to me, even in a dream?' — thus
longing for sleep, whose space is blocked by the pressure of tears from her eyes.

children.text: ādye baddhā virahadivase yā śikhā dāma hitvā
children.translated_text: The single braid she bound on the first day of separation, casting aside her hair-ornament,
that braid to be unbound by me when the curse ends and grief has fallen away —
she strokes it again and again with nails left untrimmed, painful to the touch,
that stiff, unkempt single braid, rough against the curve of her cheek, with her hand.
The rays of the moon, cool as nectar, entering through the latticed window —
approached at first with old affection, then turned away again just so,
covering her eyes, weary with sorrow, with lashes heavy with tears —

children.text: sābhre 'hnīva sthalakamalinīṃ na prabuddhāṃ na suptām
children.translated_text: like a lotus pond on a cloudy day, neither fully awake nor asleep.
That frail woman, having set aside her ornaments, wearing only soft garments,
laying her body again and again upon the lap of the bed, in the misery of misery,

children.text: tvām apy asraṃ navajalamayaṃ mocayiṣyaty avaśyaṃ
children.translated_text: will surely move even you to shed tears of fresh rainwater —
for almost everyone whose inner self is tender becomes disposed to compassion.

children.text: jāne sakhyās tava mayi manaḥ saṃbhṛtasneham asmād
children.translated_text: I know my beloved's heart holds deep affection for me, therefore
I imagine her condition thus in this first separation.

children.text: vācālaṃ māṃ na khalu subhagaṃmanyabhāvaḥ karoti
children.translated_text: It is not conceit that makes me so eloquent —

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ te nikhilam acirād bhrātar uktaṃ mayā yat
children.translated_text: all that I have said, O brother, will soon be evident to you in person.
Her eye, its sidelong glance obstructed by disheveled hair, devoid of collyrium's luster,
its brow-play forgotten even from the rejection of wine —

children.text: tvayy āsanne nayanam uparispandi śaṅke mṛgākṣyā
children.translated_text: when you draw near, I suspect that trembling eye of the doe-eyed one
will attain the beauty of a quivering blue lotus stirred by a fish.
And her left thigh, released from the nail-marks of my hands,
the familiar net of pearls cast off by the decree of fate,
that thigh, fit for the caress of my hands after lovemaking,
smooth and fair as a juicy plantain stem, will tremble.

children.text: tasmin kāle jalada yadi sā labdhanidrāsukhā syād
children.translated_text: At that hour, O cloud, if she has found the comfort of sleep,
attend upon her silently, restraining your thunder, and endure for but one watch.

children.text: mā bhūd asyāḥ praṇayini mayi svapnalabdhe kathaṃ cit
children.translated_text: Let it not happen that she, having somehow found her lover in a dream —
in a tight embrace, arms entwined like vines around his neck, suddenly broken —
rouse her then with a breeze cooled by your own dewdrops,
along with the fresh fragrance of <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) blossoms through the lattice;
as she stands at the window where you preside, her eyes still and wide with lightning within you,
begin to address that offended woman with words of steady thunder.

children.text: bhartur mitraṃ priyam avidhave viddhi mām ambuvāhaṃ
children.translated_text: 'O faithful wife, know me to be a cloud, the dear friend of your husband,
come to your presence bearing his message held in my heart,

children.text: yo vṛndāni tvarayati pathi śrāmyatāṃ proṣitānāṃ
children.translated_text: I who hasten the steps of those who toil upon the road, longing for those far away.'
with deep, tender sounds, eager to undo the braids of young women.
Thus addressed, like <s>Sītā</s> turning her face toward <s>Hanumān</s>, she,
her heart heaving with longing upon seeing you and honoring you,

children.text: śroṣyaty asmāt param avahitā saumya sīmantinīnāṃ
children.translated_text: will listen henceforth with rapt attention, O gentle one — for among faithful wives

children.text: kāntodantaḥ suhṛdupanataḥ saṃgamāt kiṃ cid ūnaḥ
children.translated_text: tidings of a husband brought by a friend are but slightly less than union itself.

children.text: tām āyuṣman mama ca vacanād ātmanaś copakartuṃ
children.translated_text: O long-lived one, to help her and to convey my words as well,
speak thus: 'Your companion, dwelling at the hermitage on <s>Rāmagiri</s>,

children.text: avyāpannaḥ kuśalam abale pṛcchati tvāṃ viyuktaḥ
children.translated_text: sends you his greetings, O gentle one, safe though separated from you —
this indeed is the first thing to be wished for among beings for whom calamity is ever near.'

children.text: aṅgenāṅgaṃ tanu ca tanunā gāḍhataptena taptaṃ
children.translated_text: Limb upon limb, my slender body upon your slender body, the fevered upon the deeply fevered,
tearful upon tearful, ceaselessly longing upon the longing,
my hot sighs upon yours that sigh still more — though far away,

children.text: saṃkalpais tair viśati vidhinā vairiṇā ruddhamārgaḥ
children.translated_text: he enters you through these imaginings, his path blocked by hostile fate.

children.text: śabdākhyeyaṃ yad api kila te yaḥ sakhīnāṃ purastāt
children.translated_text: That which, though expressible in words, he used to whisper eagerly in your ear
before your companions, out of his desire to touch your face —
he, now gone beyond the range of hearing and unseen by your eyes,
speaks this to you through my mouth, his words composed by longing:
In dark rainclouds I see your body, in the glance of a startled doe your gaze,
in the moon the beauty of your face, in the heavy tail-plumes of peacocks your hair,
in the slender ripples of rivers I see the play of your brows —

children.text: hantaikasthaṃ kva cid api na te caṇḍi sādṛśyam asti
children.translated_text: alas, O passionate one, nowhere is your complete likeness found in any single thing.
Having drawn you on a rock with mineral pigments, angered by love,

children.text: ātmānaṃ te caraṇapatitaṃ yāvad icchāmi kartum
children.translated_text: whenever I wish to paint myself fallen at your feet,

children.text: asrais tāvan muhur upacitair dṛṣṭir ālupyate me
children.translated_text: my vision is blurred again and again by tears that well up;

children.text: krūras tasminn api na sahate saṃgamaṃ nau kṛtāntaḥ
children.translated_text: even in that, cruel fate does not permit our union.
When in dream-visions I somehow obtain you, and reach out my arms

children.text: labdhāyās te katham api mayā svapnasaṃdarśaneṣu
children.translated_text: into the sky, yearning for a pitiless embrace,

children.text: paśyantīnāṃ na khalu bahuśo na sthalīdevatānāṃ
children.translated_text: it is not seldom that the forest goddesses who witness this
shed tear-drops as large as pearls upon the young shoots of trees.
Having just split open the leaf-sheaths of <s>devadāru</s> (Himalayan cedar) trees,
the southern winds that blow fragrant with their oozing resin —
I embrace those winds, O virtuous one, thinking

children.text: pūrvaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ yadi kila bhaved aṅgam ebhis taveti
children.translated_text: that perhaps they have previously touched your body.

children.text: saṃkṣipyeta kṣaṇa iva kathaṃ dīrghayāmā triyāmā
children.translated_text: 'How might the long three-watched night be compressed into a mere moment?'

children.text: sarvāvasthāsv ahar api kathaṃ mandamandātapaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: 'How might the day too, in all conditions, have but faint, feeble sunshine?'
Thus does my mind, O you of restless eyes, entertain impossible desires,
rendered shelterless by the burning pangs of separation from you.

children.text: nanv ātmānaṃ bahu vigaṇayann ātmanā nāvalambe
children.translated_text: 'Surely, valuing myself highly, I do not sustain myself by my own strength alone;'

children.text: tat kalyāṇi tvam api sutarāṃ mā gamaḥ kātaratvam
children.translated_text: therefore, O blessed one, do not you too fall into excessive despondency.

children.text: kasyātyantaṃ sukham upanataṃ duḥkham ekāntato vā
children.translated_text: For whom has unbroken happiness come, or unbroken sorrow?

children.text: nīcair gacchaty upari ca daśā cakranemikrameṇa
children.translated_text: Fortune moves low and high in turn, like the rim of a wheel.
My curse will end when <s>Viṣṇu</s>, bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, rises from his serpent-couch;

children.text: māsān anyān gamaya caturo locane mīlayitvā
children.translated_text: pass the remaining four months with eyes closed in patience.

children.text: paścād āvāṃ virahaguṇitaṃ taṃ tam ātmābhilāṣaṃ
children.translated_text: Thereafter we two shall fulfill each and every desire of the heart, intensified by separation,
in nights illumined by the moonlight of the mature autumn.

children.text: bhūyaś cāha tvam asi śayane kaṇṭhalagnā purā me
children.translated_text: And again he says: 'You once clung to my neck upon the bed,

children.text: nidrāṃ gatvā kim api rudatī sasvaraṃ viprabuddhā
children.translated_text: and having fallen asleep, you woke weeping aloud for some reason;

children.text: sāntarhāsaṃ kathitam asakṛt pṛcchataś ca tvayā me
children.translated_text: when I asked you repeatedly, you told me with a suppressed smile:

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ svapne kitava ramayan kām api tvaṃ mayeti
children.translated_text: "I saw you in a dream, O rogue — making love to some other woman."'
Learning from this token of recognition that I am well,

children.text: mā kaulīnād asitanayane mayy aviśvāsinī bhūḥ
children.translated_text: do not, O dark-eyed one, out of womanly propriety, be distrustful of me.

children.text: snehān āhuḥ kim api virahe hrāsinas te hy abhogād
children.translated_text: They say that love, though it seems to wane in separation through lack of enjoyment,
in truth, enriched in savor for the beloved object, becomes a flood of affection.

children.text: kac cit saumya vyavasitam idaṃ bandhukṛtyaṃ tvayā me
children.translated_text: O gentle one, will you undertake this task of a kinsman for me?

children.text: pratyādeśān na khalu bhavato dhīratāṃ kalpayāmi
children.translated_text: I do not presume your composure to be due to refusal;
even without being asked, you give water to the <s>cātaka</s> birds, though silently —
for the true response to those who are dear is simply the fulfillment of their desired purpose.
Having performed this kindness for me, who have taken the path of an improper request,

children.text: sauhārdād vā vidhura iti vā mayy anukrośabuddhyā
children.translated_text: whether out of friendship, or out of a compassionate thought that I am wretched —

children.text: iṣṭān deśān vicara jalada prāvṛṣā saṃbhṛtaśrīr
children.translated_text: wander through your beloved lands, O cloud, your glory replenished by the rains;

children.text: mā bhūd evaṃ kṣaṇam api ca te vidyutā viprayogaḥ
children.translated_text: may there never be, even for a moment, separation from your lightning.
